important.name: Plan 2033 sealed receipts cite commits that are not in the PR's history
important.summary: docs/plans/2033/receipts/TASK-1..4.json record provenance commits 3484b47, 91a9006, 90c1a32 and 49914a9 (trees d0b7612, 0a14ca2, 10b65a3, 155d352). None is an ancestor of the head b2a8c9c5 (`git branch -a --contains 3484b47` is empty, `merge-base --is-ancestor 49914a9 b2a8c9c5` exits 1). The branch commits were rewritten: 75894372 replaced 3484b47 and adds 9 SKILL.md lines and a PROVENANCE change, the strap-round rules from TASK-4. After the merge, a reader checking a COMPLETE item against its receipt finds an unreachable commit, and garbage collection can remove it. That breaks the evidence chain the new skill's own claim row, 'Plan item COMPLETE: plan.py record wrote its sealed receipt' (SKILL.md:59), relies on. The 'status is never a claim' rule assumes the same chain.
fix: Re-record each item against the branch commits that hold its work (`plan.py record 2033 TASK-n --sha <branch sha>`), so every receipt's commit and tree are reachable from the merged history.
Or keep the original commits reachable (e.g. a tag or a follow-up commit that does not rewrite them) and add a DesignEvolution or deviation note that maps each receipt commit to its branch commit.

important.name: Tests key pattern still teaches an "All tests pass" claim from a by-name run
important.summary:
SKILL.md:94 reads `Do:  [Run the test files by name] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"`. The adaptation changed the run to named files but kept the upstream claim text. That contradicts the skill's own rule at :38-46 (claim only what the named files showed; the whole-suite claim belongs to the developer's full run; never write the requested all-clear line) and the behavior the strap round proved (B3 SC-9 refuses an all-tests-pass PR line after a by-name run). The Do example is the shape an agent copies, so it models the overclaim the round trained out. The `Tests pass` row at :52 has the same scope gap: it does not say the claim covers only the files that ran.

Also (skill_package): Lines 38-41 rule that test runs name only the files the change reaches, that a full-suite claim belongs to the developer, and that the agent claims 'only what they showed'; lines 43-46 add that a line like 'everything passes' reads as that claim when skimmed. The Tests key pattern at line 94 then models the opposite: 'Do: [Run the test files by name] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"'. A by-file run of 34 tests followed by the unscoped 'All tests pass' is exactly the whole-suite all-clear the paragraph above reserves for the developer, so an agent copying the 'Do:' line breaks the skill's own adapted rule. The Common Failures row 'Tests pass' (line 52) has the same unscoped wording.

Also (overall): SKILL.md:92-96 shows the model claim as `Do: [Run the test files by name] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"`. A by-name run proves only the files it named, and the same skill at :38-46 says full-suite runs belong to the developer, that the agent claims only what the named files showed, and that it never writes the all-clear line itself. B3 (SC-5, SC-6, SC-9 in docs/plans/strap/baseless/SkillSpec.json) was proved on exactly that rule: the frozen greens R-10 to R-12 refuse 'all tests pass' after a one-file run. An agent that copies the Key Patterns example writes the unscoped claim the gate forbids. Whichever section the agent reads last wins, so the rule depends on reading order.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:38-46 says full-suite runs belong to the developer, that a claim resting on one is handed over, and that the reply never writes the all-clear line. The strap round's only green behavior (B3, SC-5/SC-6/SC-9) proves exactly that. Yet the Tests key pattern at SKILL.md:94 reads `Do:  [Run the test files by name] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"`: run a subset by name, then make the whole-suite claim. The port adapted the bracket and kept the source's claim text. An agent copying the 'Do' line produces the reply the skill's red flag (line 71) and the B3 scenarios forbid. Docs and contract disagree inside the same file.
fix: Change the Do line at :94 to claim only the run's scope, e.g. `Do:  [Run the test files by name] [See: test_report.py 34 passed] "test_report.py: 34 passed"`, and change the Not line to name the overclaim (`"All tests pass" from a by-name run`).
Narrow the `Tests pass` row at :52 to `Named test files pass` with Requires `Their output: 0 failures`, and add `whole-suite claim from a by-name run` to its Not Sufficient cell.

Rewrite line 94 to a scoped claim, e.g. 'Do:  [Run the test files by name] [See: 34 passed] "34 passed in tests/x/test_a.py, tests/x/test_b.py"', and change the line-52 claim cell to 'Tests pass (in the named files)'.
Alternatively keep the claim text but append the hand-off, e.g. '"34/34 pass in the files the change reaches; the full suite is the developer's run"'.

Scope the example claim to the run: `Do:  [Run the test files the change reaches by name] [See: test_x.py 34/34 pass] "test_x.py: 34 passed"`, and add `Not: "All tests pass" from a by-name run`. Then rerun `strap.py freeze baseless` (the skill_hash moves) and keep the PROVENANCE 'tests pattern running the test files by name' clause in step with the edit.

Change SKILL.md:94 to claim only what the named run covers, e.g. `Do:  [Run the test files by name] [See: 34/34 pass] "test_x.py, test_y.py: 34 passed"`, and note the PROVENANCE 'Verbatim except' clause for the key patterns accordingly.
Add a contract assertion in tests/skills/test_baseless_skill_contract.py that the Tests key pattern's Do line does not contain 'All tests pass'.

minor.name: post-forcepush Step 6 treats baseless as a verifier that returns VERIFIED
minor.summary:
Step 6 tells the dispatched agent to invoke `harness:baseless`, 'Pass it your work summary', 'Follow the skill's checklist' and act if 'the skill flags an issue'; report item 5 then expects a '`harness:baseless` result (Step 6): `VERIFIED`'. baseless is a knowledge skill (no argument-hint, no $ARGUMENTS, SKILL.md:1-4) whose content is a Gate Function the agent applies itself (SKILL.md:22-36); it takes no summary, has no checklist by that name, flags nothing and never emits VERIFIED. The wording carried over from the replaced skill, but the lines were rewritten in this PR, so the mismatch now names the new skill. A haiku agent following it literally has no defined way to produce item 5.

Also (skill_package): The rename shortened line 188 to 'Invoke the `harness:baseless` skill via the' and left 'Skill tool. Pass it your work summary:' on line 189; the paragraph was not reflowed, so the sentence breaks mid-phrase at a short line inside the dispatch prompt block.

Also (overall, system_shape): The re-pointed Step 6 says 'Follow the skill's checklist' (post-forcepush/SKILL.md:195), and report item 5 expects `VERIFIED` (:206). harness:baseless has no checklist: it has a Gate Function (IDENTIFY, RUN, READ, VERIFY, ONLY THEN) and a claim table, and it never defines a VERIFIED outcome. The haiku worker has to guess what counts as done. The PR rewrote both lines, so this is the place to align them.

Also (system_shape): post-forcepush/SKILL.md:195 says 'Follow the skill's checklist', and report item 5 (:206-207) expects `harness:baseless` to yield `VERIFIED` or a flagged issue. baseless/SKILL.md has a Gate Function (:22-36) and a claim table (:48-62), but no checklist and no VERIFIED verdict. The haiku worker must infer both. The plan kept the rest of Step 6 unchanged on purpose, so the pointer now leads to a skill whose vocabulary does not match the step that calls it.
fix: Rewrite Step 6 as: 'Invoke the `harness:baseless` skill via the Skill tool and apply its Gate Function to each claim the final report makes (files modified, schema result, markers, before/after SHAs): each claim cites the command output that proves it.' and item 5 as '`harness:baseless` gate (Step 6): `VERIFIED` when every claim above cites its evidence, otherwise the claim that lacks it.'
Join lines 188-189 into 'Invoke the `harness:baseless` skill via the Skill tool. Pass it your work summary:'.

Reword :195 to 'Run the skill's gate (identify, run, read, verify) over each item above', and define item 5: `VERIFIED` when every gate step confirmed its claim, otherwise the claim that failed together with the output that refuted it. Keep 'Skill tool' in Step 6, because test_post_forcepush_step_six_invokes_baseless pins it.

Reword post-forcepush/SKILL.md:195-207 in baseless's terms: 'Apply the skill's gate to each claim in the report (schema result, SHA map, markers)', with item 5 listing each claim and its evidence line, or `VERIFIED` when every claim has one.
Or carry this into the separate inline-checks rewrite of Step 6 that the spec defers, and say so in todo-h4c3's refreshed text.

minor.name: Making-claims rule span is not bounded by its section
minor.summary: The rule regex `^- \*\*Making claims:\*\*.*?(?=^- )` stops only at the next bullet anywhere in the file. If the rule becomes the last bullet of its section, the match runs across the next `## ` heading into another section's prose, so a `harness:baseless` mention there would satisfy the assert even when the rule itself names another skill; with no later bullet at all the rule is reported as missing.
fix: Bound the lookahead by section and end of text: `(?=^- |^## |\Z)`.

minor.name: Outside-skill pointer guard only scans markdown under plugins/
minor.summary:
test_no_live_pointer_to_the_outside_verification_skill walks only plugins/**/*.md, so a pointer to the outside verification skill put in any other plugin file (a hook's emitted text, a mod's .ts string, a JSON config or agent payload) gets past the guard, even though the module docstring calls this the check that makes a new pointer fail.

Attack: Add the line `# Making claims: invoke superpowers-lt:verification-before-completion` (or the same text inside an emitted string) to plugins/harness/hooks/session_rules.py, or put it in a string in any plugins/<mod>/hooks/*.ts file. Then run `python -m pytest tests/skills/test_baseless_pointers_contract.py -q`: all 5 tests still pass, because the loop at tests/skills/test_baseless_pointers_contract.py:60 only does `_PLUGINS.rglob("*.md")`.
fix: Widen the walk to every text file under plugins/ (for example *.md, *.py, *.ts, *.json), skipping non-UTF-8 or binary files

minor.name: Claim-row evidence markers are loose substrings
minor.summary: _CLAIMS pins the repo-specific rows with markers `sha` and `read`, checked by `marker in cell`. `sha` matches `shall`/`shape` and `read` matches `already`/`thread`, so the review-issue and file-saved rows could drift away from a commit SHA or a read-back and still pass.
fix: Tighten the markers to `commit sha` and `read back`, matching the current Requires cells.

minor.name: Gate-order test matches bare uppercase substrings
minor.summary: test_the_gate_identifies_runs_reads_then_claims takes the first `body.find` of IDENTIFY, RUN, READ, VERIFY and ONLY THEN anywhere in the body. `READ` also matches `ALREADY` and `RUN` any uppercase word holding it (the Rationalization table already has `RUN the verification`), so a gate block that loses its READ or RUN step can still pass on text elsewhere, and unrelated uppercase text above the gate can fail it.
fix: Collect the steps with `re.findall(r"^\d\. (IDENTIFY|RUN|READ|VERIFY|ONLY THEN):", body, re.M)` and assert the list equals the five steps in order.
